tasks.title: Durable job queue (lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware, priority, cap)
tasks.notes: Postgres-backed. Lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware scheduling, priority lanes, per-tenant cap.

prep.what: Build the Postgres-backed durable job queue the M3 sweeper will run on — atomic leasing, heartbeat, reclaim of stale jobs, scheduling within work windows, priority ordering, and a per-tenant cap.
prep.understand: A durable queue lives or dies on two things: atomicity (no double-dispatch when two workers race for the same job) and heartbeat/reclaim (what happens when a worker dies mid-job and the lease sits unclaimed). The window-awareness means the queue won't dispatch outside Haniel's configured work window. Per-tenant cap prevents one noisy project from starving others.
approach: Implement atomic lease acquisition using `UPDATE jobs SET status='leased', lease_expires_at=now()+interval, last_heartbeat_at=now() WHERE id=(SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE status='queued' AND dispatch_after<=now() ORDER BY priority DESC, created_at ASC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING *` — one atomic statement, no SELECT-then-UPDATE race.

Build the heartbeat updater (periodic `UPDATE ... SET last_heartbeat_at=now() WHERE id=$1 AND status='leased'`) and the reclaimer job (cron that re-queues rows WHERE `status='leased' AND lease_expires_at < now()`).

Add the per-tenant cap check (`SELECT COUNT(*) WHERE tenant_id=$1 AND status='leased' >= cap_limit`) as a pre-dispatch gate, and the window-awareness check against the config `work_window` before any dispatch.
resources: VPS `todos_platform` Postgres schema and existing `db/migrate.ts` migration runner
Claude-todos-skill `docs/specs/WORKFLOW-USER-STORY.md` for the queue's role in the pipeline
The `SWEEPER_STATE_DIR` marker pattern from t28 go-live hardening for state management reference

tasks.title: Sweeper (per-repo sandbox, quality gate incl render+screenshot)

prep.what: Build the sweeper — the autonomous code-change executor that picks a job from the queue, runs the proposed change inside a Docker repo sandbox, runs the full quality gate (tests, compile, lint, build, render, screenshot, no new console errors, write-test check), and marks done or failed.
prep.understand: The sweeper is the M3 milestone's payoff. It must: (1) pick up a leased job from the queue (t20), (2) check out the repo in an isolated Docker container via the RefreshRunners seam, (3) apply the change from the payload, (4) run each quality gate step in sequence and capture output, (5) only mark DONE if ALL gates pass — any failure requeues or marks failed. The daemon-side cross-process refresh lock (t29) is the prereq for running against live SWEEPER_REPOS; until t29 is done, test against a frozen test repo. The go-live hardening (t28, already done) gives you the `refreshAndCheckBase` + prepareOutputs freshness checking for free.
approach: Build `sweeper/runner.ts`: takes a job from the queue (lease acquired), reads the repo mapping from SWEEPER_REPOS, calls `refreshAndCheckBase` (from t28) to ensure a fresh base, then runs the change in the Docker sandbox via the injected RefreshRunners seam.

Implement each quality gate step as a named, sequential check: `runTests` → `compile` → `lint` → `build` → `renderCheck` (headless Playwright screenshot) → `consoleErrCheck` (zero new console.error lines vs baseline) → `writeTestCheck` (verify a test was added for the change).
Wire the sweeper to the durable queue (t20): on failure, transition the job to `failed` with captured output; on success, mark `done` and emit a completion event to the decision inbox.
Test end-to-end using the Module-project recipe (which already has a `prepareCommands` defined from the t28 go-live hardening work).
resources: The `refreshAndCheckBase` function and `RefreshRunners` seam from t28 (go-live hardening, already shipped)
`SWEEPER_REPOS` env config and the Module-project recipe for `prepareCommands`/`prepareOutputs`
`SWEEPER_STATE_DIR` marker convention for tracking fresh/stale state outside the git tree
Playwright pre-installed at `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium` for the render/screenshot gate
Existing sweeper subsystem tests (50 passing from t28) as regression baseline

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Harborview demo caught this: outlined-text firms have zero live-text labels. Opt-in AI tiles lane (~4.3min/sheet, costs money). MINIMAX_AI key must reach the VPS.

prep.what: Productize the M3 tiles vision lane so firms that outline all text (like Harborview) can get AI-read room labels — and add a callout-vs-room filter to stop general notes and stair arrows from polluting room names.
prep.understand: The core problem: PDFTron-based firms outline their text as vector paths, so `engine/labels.py`'s live-text extraction returns 0 words. The fix (already proven in the spike `run_labels_m3tiles.py`) is to tile the rendered floor plan image and send each tile to a vision model that reads room names visually. It works but costs money (~4.3 min/sheet via MiniMax M3 vision), so it ships as an opt-in action, not auto. Separately, Holabird shows noise: 'UP', 'FEC', multi-line general notes are being matched as room names — the callout filter kills these before they reach the workbook.
approach: Wire the `run_labels_m3tiles.py` spike logic into the service as a new route: `POST /sheets/{id}/labels/ai` (or an `?lane=m3tiles` param on the existing labels route) that fires only when explicitly requested — this is the `§7a metered-credits` event that tracks per-sheet AI cost.

Move the `MINIMAX_AI_KEY` env var into the VPS `.env` (`/opt/takeoff-engine/.env`, chmod 600) alongside the existing `API_KEYS_RAW` — same secrets pattern from the t11/t13 deploy; restart the lean docker-compose after adding it.

Build the callout-vs-room filter in `engine/labels.py`: blocklist patterns (all-caps single words like `UP`/`DN`/`FEC`/`AFF`, paragraphs longer than 25 chars, symbols starting with arrows or numbers+`'`) applied before labels reach the workbook — validate against the Holabird known-noise list in the notes.
Add a service pytest that mocks the MiniMax call and verifies the `§7a` metered-credits event fires exactly once per call, and that the callout filter drops the documented Holabird noise patterns.
resources: `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` — the existing proven spike to productize
`engine/labels.py` — existing live-text lane to extend with the `m3tiles` path
VPS `/opt/takeoff-engine/.env` — where MINIMAX_AI_KEY goes (SSH to azteam-vps, same pattern as API_KEYS_RAW from t13)
Harborview demo logs and the R13 documented noise list (FEC callouts, 'UP' arrows, general-note paragraphs) for filter patterns
MiniMax vision API docs at `api.minimax.io` — same key you already use for the triage agent

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: assemblies-lite already scaffolded in engine/assemblies.py. Full version = room type → assemblies + formulas + heights (up to 8 quantities per room, CSI libraries). The last pillar before estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Expand `engine/assemblies.py` from the lite scaffold into a full room-type → quantities engine: given a classified room type and wall height, produce up to 8 sub-quantities (paint area, drywall sq ft, flooring sq ft, ceiling sq ft, trim linear feet, etc.) and land them as rows in the Excel workbook.
prep.understand: The lite scaffold (`assemblies.py`) is already in place from the B1 work — it has the structure but not the rules. The full version needs: (1) a room-type → assembly rule table (classification → list of {quantity_type, formula, unit, CSI_code}), (2) wall height as an input (already patchable via `PATCH /measurements/{id}` with `wall_height_ft`, defaults to 9 ft if unset), (3) derived quantity formulas (e.g., paint area = perimeter × height, flooring = SF from the engine polygon, ceiling = SF). These flow into the Excel's 5-tab workbook via `engine/excel.py` — either a new 'Assemblies' tab or inline per-room columns on the existing areas tab.
approach: In `engine/assemblies.py`, build the rule table as a Python dict: `ASSEMBLY_RULES = {'BEDROOM': [{'name': 'Paint Area', 'formula': lambda r: r.perimeter_ft * r.wall_height_ft, 'unit': 'SF', 'csi': '09 91 00'}, ...], 'KITCHEN': [...], ...}`. Cover at minimum: BEDROOM, BATHROOM, KITCHEN, LIVING_ROOM, CORRIDOR, OFFICE. Use 9 ft as the default wall height.
Thread `wall_height_ft` from the `Measurement` DB row into the formula engine: `measurement.wall_height_ft or 9.0` — it's already on the model from t8's PATCH route.
Add an 'Assemblies' tab to `engine/excel.py` (or columns on Tab 1): one row per room × assembly type. Columns: Room Name, Classification, Quantity Type, Formula, Value, Unit, CSI Code.
Add pytest assertions on quantity math for 3–4 known room types (e.g., a 12×14 bedroom at 9 ft = 169.33 SF paint, 168 SF floor, 168 SF ceiling) to lock the formulas.
resources: `engine/assemblies.py` — the lite scaffold to expand (already in the repo)
`engine/excel.py` — the 5-tab workbook builder to add the Assemblies output to
The `Measurement` model schema in `service/models.py` — `wall_height_ft` field, `perimeter_ft`, and polygon SF
CSI MasterFormat Division 09 (Finishes) for csi codes: paint = 09 91 00, flooring = 09 60 00, drywall = 09 29 00
Service pytest suite (19 passing from t8) as regression baseline; `gauntlet` for the engine layer
